argument_summary: Certification is not cleanly supportable as full compliance on the current record, but it is supportable as a narrowly framed, reversible launch decision with an explicitly recorded governance gap. The admissible evidence supports aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 7% rollout with rollback and monitoring. The same record also shows the developer-support migration segment remains exposed, is below target, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. The strongest defensible packet therefore narrows the claim: do not treat rollout controls as curing the disclosure issue; treat them as limiting operational risk while documenting that certification proceeds with a specific unresolved model-card weakness.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalating this from a caveated packet to a full stop would impose launch-delay cost even though the admissible evidence shows the launch is limited, reversible, monitored, and operationally above aggregate readiness threshold. A bounded caveat preserves audit accuracy without overstating the operational significance of the unresolved disclosure issue.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy does not allow rollout controls alone to satisfy the requirement where the affected use case remains exposed and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. Public model-card and AI-risk guidance support monitoring, measurement, and documentation practices, but they do not override that release-policy predicate. The supportable policy position is therefore caveated compliance at most: operational controls mitigate launch risk, while the disclosure or approval condition remains unmet and must be recorded as an exception.
concessions: The developer-support migration segment remains eligible for the initial rollout cohort and is below target on API migration guidance.
The available risk-acceptance document is only a draft, has no approver recorded, and does not address the exposed developer-support migration segment.
Under the stated policy, rollback, dashboards, and a 7% initial rollout do not by themselves remove the disclosure duty while that segment remains exposed.
The current record does not support calling the certification clean compliance.
